behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: The hard training prefix-transition hit rate Q_l per RQ level, plus the per-level mean latent norm rho_l. Both are aggregate scalars over the training split, not per-item weights and not a loss term.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the training split only. For each training session, consecutive item pairs (i_t, i_{t+1}) with i_t != i_{t+1} form the directed edge multiset; a fixed hash subsample of at most 2^20 edges is frozen once at the start of training and reused. At every 5th epoch the current hard SID table is applied to both endpoints of every sampled edge and Q_l is the indicator average 1[p_l(i) == p_l(j)] for l = 1..L. rho_l is the mean over the 24556 training items of the Euclidean norm of the level-l residual input, taken with stop-gradient. Both are recomputed from the current encoder and codebooks, so the signal tracks the partition as it moves.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: Only the training split's user-item sequences are read; no validation or test interaction is ever loaded into the Q_l or rho_l computation, and the statistic depends only on aggregate counts over training items. Nothing per-user is stored or attached to a SID, so there is no path by which a held-out interaction could influence an item's code. The curvature scalars are global per level, hence cannot memorise an evaluation item. SID construction, the curvature update and the commitment term never see the Stage 3 prompt construction or the recall harness.

implementation_cost.claim: declared cost of the frozen run
implementation_cost.value: No new parameters and no extra forward pass over the encoder. Extra per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, K=256, L=3): the level-l assignment now costs N*K = 6.29e6 curved distance evaluations instead of a dot product, i.e. 1.89e7 pairs per forward and roughly 5.7e7 with the backward, about 6-8 flops-equivalents each (two inner products, three norms, one artanh, one division) versus one inner product before. On the same GPU family this is +8 to +20 ms per step on top of a transformer step that is already tens to hundreds of ms; over 24 steps x 3000 epochs = 72000 steps that is +10 to +24 minutes of wall clock per card (the four data-parallel cards each pay it, so the run length grows by that amount, roughly 1-3 percent of Stage 2). The statistic pass is one reduction over at most 2^20 frozen edges every 5 epochs = 600 passes at about 5 ms each, under 5 s total. Memory grows only by caching one (N x d) latent per level for the norm statistics.

implementation_cost.value: Frozen scale, B = ceil(24556/24) = 1023 items per step, L levels, C codes per level, latent d = 32, K neighbours. behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the Stage-2 training split only. For each consecutive pair (u_t, u_{t+1}) in each training sequence (optionally with gap <= 3), increment N[u_t, u_{t+1}]. Rows with fewer than 20 total transitions are masked.

The successor table is frozen per refresh block and never uses a validation/test target, so no validation or test interaction can influence a codeword position or an aperture.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Q_l is pinned so that c_l = 1.0 for every level; the code executes the identical exp_0^c and d_c at unit negative curvature, so geometry is present but no longer driven by transitions. This arm isolates the feedback loop, not the geometry.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Q_l measured from training transitions, c_l derived and smoothed as specified, level-l assignment and commitment evaluated with exp_0^{c_l} and d_{c_l}. This is the only arm trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c_l := 0, exp_0^0 is the identity and d_0 is squared Euclidean in the same code, while Q_l is still computed and logged. Behaviour exists but has no geometric channel, so this arm isolates whether the curvature is doing the work.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only. For each training session, consecutive item pairs (i_t, i_{t+1}) with i_t != i_{t+1} form the directed edge multiset; a fixed hash subsample of at most 2^20 edges is frozen once at the start of training and reused. At every 5th epoch the current hard SID table is applied to both endpoints of every sampled edge and Q_l is the indicator average 1[p_l(i) == p_l(j)] for l = 1..L. rho_l is the mean over the 24556 training items of the Euclidean norm of the level-l residual input, taken with stop-gradient. Both are recomputed from the current encoder and codebooks, so the signal tracks the partition as it moves.
ideas.behavior_signal: The hard training prefix-transition hit rate Q_l per RQ level, plus the per-level mean latent norm rho_l. Both are aggregate scalars over the training split, not per-item weights and not a loss term.
ideas.cost_estimate: No new parameters and no extra forward pass over the encoder. Extra per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, K=256, L=3): the level-l assignment now costs N*K = 6.29e6 curved distance evaluations instead of a dot product, i.e. 1.89e7 pairs per forward and roughly 5.7e7 with the backward, about 6-8 flops-equivalents each (two inner products, three norms, one artanh, one division) versus one inner product before. On the same GPU family this is +8 to +20 ms per step on top of a transformer step that is already tens to hundreds of ms; over 24 steps x 3000 epochs = 72000 steps that is +10 to +24 minutes of wall clock per card (the four data-parallel cards each pay it, so the run length grows by that amount, roughly 1-3 percent of Stage 2). The statistic pass is one reduction over at most 2^20 frozen edges every 5 epochs = 600 passes at about 5 ms each, under 5 s total. Memory grows only by caching one (N x d) latent per level for the norm statistics.
ideas.coupling_equation: c_l = (1/Q_l - 1) / (rho_l^2 + 1e-8), and the level-l assignment is c_l* = argmin_k (2/sqrt(c_l)) artanh( sqrt(c_l) * || ( -exp_0^{c_l}(z_l) ) (+) exp_0^{c_l}(e_{l,k}) || ), with commitment beta * d_{c_l}( exp_0^{c_l}(z_l), exp_0^{c_l}(e_{l,c_l*}) )^2. The behaviour term is the prefix-confusion odds (1/Q_l - 1); the curved term is d_{c_l}; they meet in the single scalar c_l that multiplies the geometry.
ideas.coupling_path: training transitions -> hard SID prefixes -> Q_l and rho_l -> derived curvature c_l -> exp_0^{c_l} and d_{c_l} at level l -> argmin code index and commitment penalty -> encoder and codebook gradients -> new SID prefixes -> next epoch's Q_l. Behaviour enters only through c_l; geometry enters only through d_c and exp_0^c. Pinning Q_l (behaviour off) removes the loop; setting c_l = 0 (geometry off) makes the behaviour term inert. Either removal changes the same computation, so the pathway is genuinely joint.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the level-l prefix is the thing the generator has to predict, then making the level-l metric more negatively curved exactly when the measured prefix hit rate is low should force level-l codes to separate along the radial (hierarchical) direction rather than only by angle, so that a child prefix becomes more nearly a function of its parent prefix. This must show up as (a) Q_l rising over Stage 2 epochs while the behaviour-off arm's Q_l stays flat, (b) deeper levels receiving larger c_l because Q_l is non-increasing in l, and (c) Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 with no validation-based early stopping. The mechanism is worth keeping if the observed Q_l trend is monotone and the final recall clears the target; the Q_l trace, not recall alone, is what shows the loop actually ran.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ quantizer, at the level-l nearest-code assignment and in the level-l commitment term of the RQ-VAE objective; the codebook update itself stays Euclidean.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: The Poincaré ball of derived negative curvature kappa_l = -c_l: origin exponential map exp_0^c(z) = tanh(sqrt(c)||z||)/(sqrt(c)||z||) z, Möbius addition (+), and Poincaré distance d_c(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-u)(+)v||). c_l is a data-derived scalar per level, not a learned parameter.
ideas.key_change: At the start of every K-th epoch we measure, per RQ level l, the fraction Q_l of training directed transitions whose two endpoints share the same level-l SID prefix, plus the mean encoder latent norm rho_l. From these two measured numbers we DERIVE a positive curvature magnitude c_l, and the level-l assignment and commitment term then use the Poincaré distance of curvature -c_l (encoder output and code vectors pushed into that ball by the origin exponential map). Poorer prefix predictability at a level means a larger c_l, which stretches the ball near its boundary and forces that level's codes to separate radially instead of only angularly.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Only the training split's user-item sequences are read; no validation or test interaction is ever loaded into the Q_l or rho_l computation, and the statistic depends only on aggregate counts over training items. Nothing per-user is stored or attached to a SID, so there is no path by which a held-out interaction could influence an item's code. The curvature scalars are global per level, hence cannot memorise an evaluation item. SID construction, the curvature update and the commitment term never see the Stage 3 prompt construction or the recall harness.
ideas.motivation: A generative recommender emits a level-1 code first, then conditions on it. If the level-1 code barely predicts which level-2 code the next item carries, the generator's prefix becomes a coin flip and downstream recall collapses no matter how good the reconstruction is. Issue #126 showed that the hard prefix-transition score Q_H, computed from training-only transitions, ranks downstream test recall across seven SIDs (Spearman +0.821, exploratory). That score is currently only a DIAGNOSTIC: a proxy was built to rank prefixes, but nothing closed the loop. CURVCTRL-SID turns the hard score into the state variable of the geometry, so the quantizer's own metric is reshaped by exactly the quantity that predicts recall, at the level where the prediction fails.
ideas.novelty: All earlier mechanisms put user behaviour into a per-item quantity: successor mass, transition mass, Fréchet weights, Sinkhorn cost rows, cone/tangent directions, or a prefix-rank proxy loss term. CURVCTRL-SID adds NO loss term and NO per-item behaviour weight. It uses a single per-level SCALAR measured statistic, the hard prefix hit rate Q_l of the training transition set, as the curvature of the Poincaré metric used by that same RQ level. Curvature is therefore neither a hyperparameter nor a learned parameter: it is a closed-loop controller output, recomputed each epoch from the current SID assignment. It is also the only proposal in which the geometry VARIES ACROSS RQ LEVELS, and it is the direct answer to issue #126's open question: instead of optimising the ranking proxy, the hard score is fed back as the metric in which the next assignment is made.
ideas.observables:
- Q_l per epoch for l = 1..L: expected to rise, and expected to stay flat in the behaviour-off arm.
- c_l per epoch: expected to increase with depth (Q_l is non-increasing in l) and to track dips in Q_l.
- Stage3 test_recall@10 at the end of the frozen protocol, against the 0.065 target and the recorded baseline SID.
- Prefix behaviour predictability on training transitions under the fixed Q_H harness inherited from issue #126, recorded before and after Stage 2.
- Level-wise code usage entropy and the mean number of distinct level-2 children per level-1 code (a direct measure of whether the tree became more prefix-predictable).
- Curved commitment magnitude and the conformal factor 1/(1 - c_l ||u||^2) at the mean radius, which should rise with c_l.
- Number of items whose code index flips between consecutive epochs, which should shrink as c_l stabilises.
risks: The main failure is that Q_l is dominated by the level-1 partition and is nearly constant across epochs, so the controller produces a near-fixed curvature and the mechanism degenerates to a fixed-curvature Poincaré quantizer; the epoch-wise Q_l trace reveals this immediately. Second, a feedback loop can oscillate or collapse onto the boundary cap, mitigated by the factor-2 clamp and harmonic smoothing but not eliminated. Third, Poincaré distances saturate near the boundary, so the commitment gradient can vanish exactly where curvature is largest; the c_l cap and float64 statistics reduce but do not remove this. Fourth, the extra distances could slow Stage 2 enough to interact with the fixed epoch budget, though the estimated overhead is small. Fifth, with one run the effect is confounded with seed noise; the Q_l trajectory is the only internal evidence that the coupling did anything.
ideas.safeguards:
- All Möbius additions and artanh calls for the statistics run in float64; the batched distances run in float32 with the artanh argument clipped to 1-1e-7.
- c_l is capped by 0.99/max||z_l||^2 so no mapped point reaches the ball boundary; rho_l has a 1e-8 floor.
- c_l changes by at most a factor of 2 per update and is smoothed by a 1/10 harmonic average, so the metric cannot jump between epochs.
- Q_l is clipped to [1e-3, 1]; if Q_l == 1 for all l the curvature collapses to the floor 1e-4 and the run behaves like the Euclidean baseline, a safe degenerate mode rather than a NaN.
- Code-usage entropy per level is logged every epoch; if a level's entropy drops below 10 percent of log K the run still completes (diagnostic only, no gating).
- No parameter is initialised from behaviour and no eval-time data is touched, so checkpoint selection stays on the frozen protocol.

        E_ = exp_0^{c_l}(E_l)                    # K x d codes mapped
        D  = poincare_dist(u, E_)                # B x K, curvature -c_l
        k* = argmin(D, axis=1)
        z_{l+1} = z_l - E_l[k*]
        L_commit += 0.25 * D[b, k*]^2
      loss = L_recon + L_commit + L_codebook

      c_l   = clip(c_l + (c_raw - c_l)/min(t+1,10), c_l/2, 2*c_l)
    if not behaviour_on: c_l = 1.0
    if not geometry_on:  c_l = 0.0   # exp = id, d = squared Euclidean

  exp_0^c(z) = tanh(sqrt(c)||z||)/(sqrt(c)||z|| + 1e-12) * z
  poincare_dist(u,v):
    x = -u ; y = v
    num = (1 + 2c<x,y> + c||y||^2) x + (1 - c||x||^2) y
    den = 1 + 2c<x,y> + c^2 ||x||^2 ||y||^2
    r   = clip(sqrt(c) * ||num/den||, 0, 1 - 1e-7)

Notation: L RQ levels (L=3 in the frozen baseline), K codes per level (K=256), N=24556 training items, d latent dim.
1. Behaviour statistics, recomputed from the TRAINING split only, on epochs t where t mod K_meas == 0 (K_meas=5):
   E = observed directed transitions (i -> j, i != j, consecutive within a training session), subsampled once and frozen to at most 2^20 edges by a fixed hash of (i,j) so the same sample is reused for all epochs.
   p_l(i) = (c_1(i),...,c_l(i)) = current hard SID prefix of item i.
   Q_l = (1/|E|) * sum over (i,j) in E of 1[ p_l(i) == p_l(j) ], clipped to [Q_min, 1], Q_min = 1e-3.
   rho_l = (1/N) * sum over training items i of || z_l(i) ||_2, where z_l is the level-l residual input (stop-gradient).
2. Derived curvature, one positive scalar per level:
   c_l_raw = ( 1/Q_l - 1 ) / ( rho_l^2 + 1e-8 )
   c_l_raw = min( c_l_raw, 0.99 / ( max_i ||z_l(i)||^2 + 1e-8 ) )   [derived cap: keeps mapped points inside the ball]
   c_l_raw = max( c_l_raw, 1e-4 )                                    [documented floor for artanh stability]
3. Anti-oscillation smoothing (the only other constant, a documented harmonic average, not tuned):
   c_l <- c_l_prev + (c_l_raw - c_l_prev) / min(t + 1, 10), and c_l is additionally clipped to [c_l_prev/2, 2*c_l_prev] per update.
4. Curved operators used at level l (curvature kappa_l = -c_l):
   exp_0^c(z) = ( tanh( sqrt(c) * ||z|| ) / ( sqrt(c) * ||z|| + 1e-12 ) ) * z
   x (+) y   = ( (1 + 2c<x,y> + c||y||^2) x + (1 - c||x||^2) y ) / ( 1 + 2c<x,y> + c^2 ||x||^2 ||y||^2 )
   d_c(u,v)  = ( 2 / sqrt(c) ) * artanh( sqrt(c) * || (-u) (+) v || ), artanh argument clipped to 1 - 1e-7
5. Quantizer at level l (this replaces only the distance; the codebook update stays the baseline Euclidean/RQ update, deliberately NOT a curved Fréchet update):
   u = exp_0^{c_l}(z_l);  e_k = exp_0^{c_l}(e_{l,k})
   c_l* = argmin_k d_{c_l}(u, e_k)
   z_{l+1} = z_l - e_{l,c_l*}                        (residual stays Euclidean, standard RQ)
   L_commit += beta * d_{c_l}(u, e_{l,c_l*})^2,  beta = 0.25 (baseline value)
   Total loss = L_recon + L_commit + L_codebook, everything else unchanged.
6. Switches (must exist in code; only BOTH_ON is trained):
   behaviour_on: Q_l as measured.  behaviour_off: Q_l pinned so that c_l = 1.0 for all l (fixed unit negative curvature, no adaptation).
   geometry_on: d_c / exp_0^c with c_l.  geometry_off: c_l := 0, exp = identity, d = squared Euclidean.

ideas.title: Feedback curvature: the measured hard prefix-transition score of each RQ level sets that level's negative curvature, which then reshapes the same level's quantizer metric.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: alpha_k is replaced by the constant pi/4 for every k and S_k is replaced by K uniformly sampled other prefixes (same cardinality, no transition statistics); the geometry term is unchanged. The switch exists in code and is not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the full coupling above, behaviour-conditioned aperture and successor set evaluated with the Poincare log map and hyperbolic angle. This is the single trained candidate.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: the same behaviour-conditioned S_k and alpha_k are used, but theta is the Euclidean angle between p_{k'} - p_k and p_k, and the depth hinge uses Euclidean norms; no log map, no ball. The switch exists in code and is not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 training split only. For each consecutive pair (u_t, u_{t+1}) in each training sequence (optionally with gap <= 3), increment N[u_t, u_{t+1}]. At refresh time assign every training item i its current level-1 codeword k(i) = argmin_k d_P(enc(i), c_k), accumulate M[k,k'] += N[i,j], row-normalise q_k, keep the top K=8 successors by mass plus an "other" bucket, and compute H_k = -sum q log q over that distribution (log base e). Rows with fewer than 20 total transitions are masked.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions aggregated to first-level prefix transitions, plus the entropy of each prefix's successor distribution.
ideas.cost_estimate: One extra pass every 100 epochs over 24556 items to refresh M (O(#transitions), seconds). Per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, batch ~1023, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs): at most 256 source prefixes x 8 successors = 2048 Poincare log/angle evaluations of dimension d plus one scalar entropy per source row; this is under 1% of the RQ-VAE forward+backward flops and adds roughly 2-4% wall clock. 72000 steps total; no extra model, no extra encoder forward pass for successor items.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_cone = mean_k mean_{k' in S_k} [ relu( theta_{p_k}(p_{k'}) - alpha_k ) + relu(||p_k|| - ||p_{k'}||) ], with alpha_k = arctan(exp(H_k/log(K+1) - 1)) and theta_{p_k}(p_{k'}) = arccos( <log_{p_k}(p_{k'}), p_k> / (||log_{p_k}(p_{k'})|| ||p_k||) ).
ideas.coupling_path: behaviour -> prefix successor matrix M -> row entropy H_k -> aperture alpha_k and successor set S_k -> Poincare cone penalty on (p_k, p_k') -> gradient on level-1 codewords -> new SIDs. Removing behaviour removes alpha_k and S_k; removing geometry removes log_p and the hyperbolic angle. Either change alters the gradient on c_{1,k}, hence the assignment and the SID.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the hard Q_H-to-recall relation is causal and not a small-sample artefact, then a differentiable cone proxy that is optimised during Stage 2 should (i) raise cone containment and lower the level-1 successor rank of held-out training transitions, (ii) raise the Issue #126 hard Q_H evaluated on the resulting SID, and (iii) lift Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 with the same single run. If Q_H only correlates because both are driven by item popularity, Q_H will move but recall will not.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In Stage-2 RQ-VAE training, as an auxiliary term on the level-1 codebook (and optionally the level-2 prefix points), inside the same backward pass as the reconstruction and commitment losses, before the codebook is frozen for Stage 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c=1 Poincare ball: Riemannian log map log_p(x), hyperbolic angle between tangent vectors at p, and a geodesic entailment cone (angular aperture plus radial-depth hinge). No trainable curvature, no Lorentz model.
ideas.key_change: Build a directed level-1 prefix transition matrix from training-split item transitions, turn each row into a successor distribution, and add to the RQ-VAE objective a hyperbolic entailment-cone penalty that pushes each observed successor prefix into the cone rooted at the source prefix, with half-aperture alpha_k = arctan(exp(H_k/log(K+1) - 1)) taken from that row's entropy.
ideas.leakage_boundary: N is built only from Stage-2 training sequences; validation and test interactions are never read. Prefix assignments k(i) use only training items' encoder outputs. The successor table is frozen per refresh block and never uses a validation/test target, so no validation or test interaction can influence a codeword position or an aperture.
ideas.motivation: Issue #126 showed that the hard hyperbolic prefix score Q_H ranks with downstream test_R@10 but left open whether a differentiable version can be optimised and whether that optimisation reaches recall. The first RQ-VAE token is the coarse cluster the generator must commit to first; if the level-1 codebook is organised so that a prefix's observed successors fall inside its own curved "future cone", the first token becomes behaviourally predictive instead of only reconstruction-optimal.
ideas.novelty: The earlier rounds used successor mass inside Sinkhorn, successor-weighted Fréchet codebook updates, curved residuals, geodesic charts, Lorentz cones and branch curvature. This proposal is not a cone quantizer and not a mass-weighted assignment: it keeps the RQ-VAE quantizer unchanged and adds a behaviour-conditioned aperture to a Poincare entailment cone on the level-1 codewords, so that the aperture itself is a measured function of the training-only prefix-transition entropy (no swept constant), and the cone penalty is the differentiable proxy for the hard Q_H of Issue #126. Prefix-to-prefix pairs (not item pairs) make the whole penalty act on the codebook only.
ideas.observables: Cone containment rate of held-out training prefix transitions; level-1 branch entropy of the learned SID versus the data; successor rank of the true next prefix; the Issue #126 hard Q_H on the new SID; reconstruction loss and codebook usage; and the single-run Stage 3 test_recall@10 against the 0.065 target.
risks: The cone penalty may collapse many prefixes toward the boundary or make level-1 codes redundant, hurting reconstruction and prefix counts; behaviour sparsity (first-level prefixes with few transitions) can make entropy and aperture noisy; the aperture could be gamed by pushing entropy down instead of structuring the geometry (mitigated by stopping the gradient through alpha); the effect may be too weak at level 1 alone.
ideas.safeguards: clamp all ball points to norm <= 1 - 1e-3 before log/artanh; if ||p|| < 1e-4 use the Euclidean limit theta = arccos(<x-p,p>/(||x-p|| ||p||)); if ||log_p(x)|| < 1e-8 skip the pair; mask prefixes with fewer than 20 transitions; drop self-pairs k=k' before the depth hinge; stop the gradient through H_k and through the assignment k(i); if L_cone is non-finite or zero, skip the term for that step and log it; refresh M only from training sequences and reuse the previous M if the refresh is degenerate.
ideas.spec_equations: (1) Poincare log map, c=1: log_p(x) = (2/(1-||p||^2)) * artanh(||(-p) (+) x||) * ((-p)(+)x)/||(-p)(+)x||, with Moebius addition (+). (2) prefix point p_k = exp_0(c_{1,k}) = tanh(||c_{1,k}||) * c_{1,k}/||c_{1,k}||. (3) theta as in COUPLING EQUATION. (4) alpha_k = arctan(exp(H_k/log(K+1) - 1)), stop-gradient through H_k. (5) total loss L = L_rec + L_commit + L_codebook + lambda_b * L_cone, with lambda_b fixed once on the first batch after the encoder warm-up as lambda_b = stopgrad(L_rec)/stopgrad(L_cone), clipped to [0.01, 10], then frozen for all 3000 epochs. (6) pseudocode: every 100 epochs recompute k(i) and M; each step, sample prefixes, compute p_k, log_{p_k}(p_k'), theta, alpha, L_cone, add to the existing backward.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: level-1 codebook rows, the current item-to-prefix assignment, the training-only transition matrix, K=8, curvature c=1, batch. Outputs: a scalar L_cone and its gradient with respect to the level-1 (and optionally level-2) codebook rows; no change to the encoder output shape or to the Stage-3 interface.

specification.text: See SPEC EQUATIONS. Inputs: level-1 codebook C in R^{K x d} (K codewords, d dim), training-split transition counts N_ij, a curvature c=1 Poincare ball. Precompute once: M_kk' = sum_{i in k, j in k'} N_ij with k = prefix1(i), k' = prefix1(j) from the current codeword assignment, so M is refreshed every 100 epochs (cheap, 24.6k items). Per step: sample up to 256 source prefixes with >=20 transitions, take their top-8 successors by M mass, evaluate the cone penalty, backprop into C. No encoder or decoder change.

ideas.title: Behaviour-entropy Poincare entailment cones as a differentiable surrogate for the first-level prefix score

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: BEHAVIOUR=off sets beta_i = 0 for all items, so the exp map is the identity and the run reduces to the plain curved three-level RQ-VAE; the switch exists in code and is unit-tested, and this arm is not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: BEHAVIOUR=on and GEOMETRY=on, i.e. the single frozen run reported for this candidate: exp_{z_i}(beta_i*rhat_i) followed by Poincare assignment, Möbius residuals and Poincare reconstruction, 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards, frozen Stage-3 protocol, no early stopping, no sweep, no seed repetition.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: GEOMETRY=off keeps beta_i but replaces the curved operations by Euclidean ones: z'_i = z_i*exp(beta_i), squared Euclidean assignment, additive residual chain, Euclidean commitment; the switch exists in code and is unit-tested, and this arm is not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 training split only. Walk each training session in order, drop immediate repeats of the same item, and increment T[i,j] for every consecutive pair (i then j). Row-normalise with Laplace smoothing as above, compute H(p_i) and divide by log|Succ(i)| to obtain c_i in [0,1]. Compute cbar, sigma, gamma once and freeze beta for all 24556 items before the first epoch as an item-indexed lookup table. Items never appearing as a transition source get beta = 0.
ideas.behavior_signal: Successor entropy concentration of each item's directed training transition distribution (how diffuse versus predictable its continuation is), normalised by its successor-set size.
ideas.cost_estimate: One frozen run, one seed, no sweep. Per step the batch is 24556/24 ≈ 1023 items: 1023 exp maps (elementwise, O(d)) plus 3 × 1023 × 256 ≈ 7.9e5 Poincare distances instead of squared Euclidean ones, so the only added transcendental is arcosh on a kernel that is a small fraction of encoder/decoder cost: roughly +4 to +6 percent step time and under 5 percent of wall clock over 3000 epochs × 24 steps = 72k steps, plus a one-off beta precompute of a few seconds over the training transition pairs. Memory adds one frozen float and one unit vector per item plus one latent buffer.
ideas.coupling_equation: k1(i) = argmin_k d_P( exp_{z_i}( beta_i * rhat_i ), c_{1,k} ), with beta_i = clip(gamma*(cbar - c_i), -1, 1), gamma = clip(1/sigma_c, 0.5, 8), rhat_i = z_i/||z_i||, and d_P the curvature -1/R^2 Poincare distance. Removing the behaviour term sets beta_i = 0 so the exp map is the identity; removing the curved term replaces the exp map by a Euclidean dilation and d_P by Euclidean distance.
ideas.coupling_path: beta_i (behaviour, frozen per item) sets the geodesic step length; the exp map (geometry) turns that length into a new position z'_i; the Poincare distance from z'_i to the level-1 codebook produces k1 and hence the SID. With geometry off the same beta becomes a scalar dilation and yields different codes; with behaviour off the geometry is the identity shift and yields different codes; neither factor can be dropped without changing k1, k2, k3.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: It is worth keeping only if the encoder does not cancel the shift and the shift buys prefix sharpness. Concretely, the post-training rank correlation between beta_i and hyperbolic radius artanh(||z_i||/R) must stay clearly positive (target > 0.3; near zero means the encoder inverted the displacement and the mechanism is inert), and level-1 successor purity (share of training transitions whose endpoints share the level-1 code) must rise together with Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. If radius tracks behaviour but recall is flat, the reallocation is real but the generator cannot exploit it.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside training, on the RQ-VAE forward path between the encoder head and the first residual level; also inside quantisation, because assignment, residual chain and reconstruction all use curved distances at the same curvature. It is not a side loss and does not touch Stage 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: The Poincare exponential map at z along its radial unit geodesic, exp_z(beta*rhat) = z (+) (R*tanh(beta/(2R)) * rhat), at fixed negative curvature K = -1/R^2 with R = 0.9; the substrate uses the Poincare distance d_P(x,y) = R*arcosh(1 + 2R^2||x-y||^2 / ((R^2-||x||^2)(R^2-||y||^2))) and Möbius addition at the same curvature.
ideas.key_change: Each item gets a frozen scalar beta_i = gamma*(cbar - c_i) from the concentration of its training successor distribution; every training step moves the latent along its own radial geodesic by hyperbolic distance beta_i, z'_i = exp_{z_i}(beta_i * rhat_i), and only z'_i is quantised by the Poincare residual chain. Capacity redistributes across levels: concentrated items stay near the origin where level-1 codes live, diffuse items are pushed into the exponentially large outer region and must be resolved by levels 2-3.
ideas.leakage_boundary: T is built exclusively from interactions in the Stage-2 training split that the RQ-VAE already trains on; validation and test interactions are never read while constructing SIDs, and beta is frozen before epoch 1, so no validation- or test-derived statistic can influence a code assignment. Vocabulary and beta indices come from the training split; unseen items keep beta = 0 and are quantised as in the baseline. Stage 3 consumes the frozen SIDs and feeds nothing back into beta or the quantiser.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE level-1 prefixes are the token the generative recommender emits first, and a level-1 cell that mixes a niche item with a hub is untrainable: the cell's successor distribution is smeared by the hub, so the first token carries little information. Issue #126 established that the hard hyperbolic first-level prefix score Q_H ranks with downstream test_R@10 (Spearman +0.821 on seven SIDs), which says the geometric separation of the level-1 partition is the quantity worth changing - yet all seven SIDs shared one radial layout. Here the radial layout itself is set by a training-only behaviour statistic, so level-1 capacity is spent on items whose continuation is predictable and fine-level capacity on items whose continuation is diffuse.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds moved behaviour into the assignment mass (successor-diffused Poincare Sinkhorn), into the codebook update (successor-weighted curved Fréchet means), into per-branch and per-level curvature, into tangent/gyro targets, into Lorentz cones, into the prefix score itself, into geodesic charts and into code repair. None changed WHERE an item sits along the ball's radial geodesic as a function of behaviour. This is a per-item curved displacement (an explicit exp map along the item's own radial geodesic) applied to the latent before any assignment exists; the hyperbolic quantiser is only the substrate, and the new object is a deterministic behaviour-conditioned geodesic displacement field - not a loss term, not a codebook rule, not an assignment weight.
ideas.observables: (1) Spearman correlation between beta_i and post-training hyperbolic radius artanh(||z_i||/R), the direct signature of the coupling; (2) level-1 successor purity and the same for levels 2 and 3; (3) number of distinct level-1 codes used and level-1 usage entropy, to show capacity has not collapsed; (4) per-item SID flip rate between consecutive checkpoints; (5) Stage-3 test_recall@10. All diagnostics are recorded, none is an admission gate.

rejected_ideas.reason: out of scope: ablation_geometry_off does not say what replaces the curve

risks: The encoder controls z and can compensate the shift by pulling high-beta items inward, cancelling the effect (that is exactly why the radius-beta correlation is recorded). Pushing diffuse items outward can crowd the outer shell, inflate level-2/3 collisions and starve the mid radius, giving dead level-1 codes and a level-1 usage-entropy collapse. arcosh is numerically hostile near the boundary. Laplace-smoothed concentration is noisy for low-degree items, and sigma dominated by the many one-successor items makes gamma small and the shift weak. Finally a better prefix partition need not survive the frozen Stage-3 generator, which may simply re-learn the SID marginal.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp the arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-7; clamp both radius denominators R^2-||x||^2 to >= 1e-6 before dividing; clamp ||z|| into [1e-3 R, 0.999 R] after the encoder and after the shift so no point reaches the boundary; beta bounded by one curvature-radius unit and gamma bounded to [0.5, 8] so a degenerate sigma cannot explode the shift; fall back to z' = z when ||z|| < 1e-8 (rhat undefined); beta = 0 for items without a successor row, stored with requires_grad=False and no gradient into the statistics; curvature fixed at K = -1/R^2 with R = 0.9, so there is no curvature sweep; assert every step that max ||z'|| < R and that no NaN enters d_P.
ideas.spec_equations: Precompute (training split only): T[i,j] += 1 for consecutive (i,j) with i != j; p_i(j) = (T[i,j]+1)/(sum_j T[i,j] + |Succ(i)|); H_i = -sum_j p_i(j) log p_i(j); c_i = 1 - H_i/log|Succ(i)| for |Succ(i)| >= 2, c_i = 1 for |Succ(i)| = 1, else undefined; cbar, sigma over finite c_i; gamma = clip(1/sigma, 0.5, 8); beta_i = 0 if c_i undefined else clip(gamma*(cbar - c_i), -1, 1). Every step: u = encoder(x); z = R*u/(1+||u||); rhat = z/max(||z||,1e-8); step = R*tanh(beta_i/(2R)); z' = mobius_add(z, step*rhat); if ||z'|| > 0.999R: z' *= 0.999R/||z'||; if ||z'|| < 1e-3R: z' *= 1e-3R/max(||z'||,1e-12); r = z'; for l in 1..3: k_l = argmin_k d_P(r, c[l][k]); r = mobius_add(r, -c[l][k_l]); codes.append(k_l); zhat = mobius_add(mobius_add(c[1][k1], c[2][k2]), c[3][k3]); loss = reconstruction(decoder(zhat), x) + lambda_c * sum_l d_P(r_l, c[l][k_l])**2 / R**2 + codebook terms exactly as baseline with lambda_c and lambda_e unchanged; backprop through d_P and through z', with beta held constant (stop-gradient on the statistics).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training item sequences (Stage-2 split only) for beta; per step the encoder latent u_i, the frozen beta_i, the three 256-code ball codebooks and the curvature radius R. Outputs: the beta lookup table (24556 floats), displaced latents z'_i, SID triples (k1,k2,k3) per item, and the loss and gradients that update encoder and codebooks. The operator is deterministic given (z, beta, R) and returns a point of the same dimension strictly inside the ball.

specification.text: Fixed curvature K = -1/R^2 with R = 0.9 (documented default, never tuned). Encoder head z = R*u/(1+||u||) so ||z|| < R with no tanh saturation. Offline once, before epoch 1: directed transition counts T[i,j] from consecutive items inside training sessions only; Laplace-smoothed successor distribution p_i(j) = (T[i,j]+1)/(sum_j T[i,j] + |Succ(i)|); concentration c_i = 1 - H(p_i)/log|Succ(i)| in [0,1]; cbar, sigma = mean and std of c_i over items with at least one successor; gamma = clip(1/sigma, 0.5, 8); beta_i = clip(gamma*(cbar - c_i), -1, 1); items with no successor row get beta_i = 0. Per step: rhat_i = z_i/max(||z_i||,1e-8); z'_i = z_i (+) (R*tanh(beta_i/(2R)) * rhat_i) with Möbius addition at curvature -1/R^2; clamp ||z'_i|| into [1e-3 R, 0.999 R]; then the usual three-level chain r_1 = z'_i, k_l = argmin_k d_P(r_l, c_{l,k}), r_{l+1} = r_l (+) (-c_{l,k_l}), zhat = c_1k1 (+) c_2k2 (+) c_3k3, SID(i) = (k1,k2,k3). Loss, optimiser, learning rate, ordering, epoch count and the Stage-3 protocol are unchanged; only the quantiser's input changes. Switches: BEHAVIOUR=off sets beta_i = 0; GEOMETRY=off replaces the exp map by Euclidean dilation z_i*exp(beta_i) and d_P by squared Euclidean. Both switches exist and are unit-tested; no arm is trained with them off this round.

ideas.title: Behavioural-diffuseness geodesic pre-shift of item latents before a Poincare residual quantiser, so level-1 prefixes fill with behaviourally predictable items.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: alpha = 0 and w ≡ 0 in the consensus step so x̂_i = exp_0^kappa(z_i); Lorentzian chain, codebooks, curvature untouched. Code exists and is correct; not trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: alpha = 0.5, w from successor profiles, kappa = 1, full Lorentzian chain — this is the single trained arm.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: kappa → 0: identity lift, Euclidean consensus x̂_i = (1−alpha)z_i + alpha·Σ_j w_ij z_j over the same twins, L2 assignment, linear residual r_{l+1} = r_l − e_{l,q_l}. Code exists and is correct; not trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only, count directed gap-1 item transitions T_ij over the training sequences of the 24556 training items; row-normalise P_i· = T_i· / Σ_j T_ij (zero rows stay zero); s_ij = ⟨√P_i·, √P_j·⟩ / (‖√P_i·‖‖√P_j·‖) clipped to [0,1], with s_ii = 0; keep the top-K per item, K = round(median_i outdeg_i); w_ij = s_ij / Σ_{j'∈N_i} s_ij'. Built once, frozen, no gradient, no parameters.
ideas.behavior_signal: Successor-profile equivalence: the Hellinger/cosine similarity between the row-normalised directed-transition distributions of two items.
ideas.cost_estimate: Frozen scale, B = ceil(24556/24) = 1023 items per step, L levels, C codes per level, latent d = 32, K neighbours. Smoothing gather/combine B*K*(d+1) ≈ 1023*8*33 ≈ 2.7e5 MAC per step ≈ 1% of the existing B*L*C*d ≈ 1023*3*256*32 ≈ 2.5e7 MAC assignment. The Lorentzian assignment replaces the Euclidean one at the same order (B*L*C*(d+1) vs B*L*C*d), so step overhead is under 2% of the quantiser and under 1% of a full Stage-2 step; the epoch-start table refresh is one no-gradient encoder pass (24 batches) = +4.2% encoder forward per epoch. One-off graph build (sparse P·Pᵀ on a 24556×24556 transition matrix, ~5e5 nnz) is 1–3 min CPU, a few hundred MB, once. Over 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72k steps this is baseline + ~5% wall clock, no memory growth.
ideas.coupling_equation: x̂_i = proj_kappa( (1−alpha)·exp_0^kappa(z_i) + alpha·Σ_{j∈N_i} w_ij·exp_0^kappa(z_j) ), and q_1(i) = argmin_k d_H( exp_0^kappa(r_1(i)), e_{1,k} )² with r_1(i) = log_0^kappa(x̂_i); w_ij is the behaviour term (successor-profile mass) and exp_0/log_0/d_H are the curved terms, in the same expression.
ideas.coupling_path: training transitions → successor-profile twins and weights w → Minkowski combination of the item's and its twins' hyperboloid points → re-projected point → log_0 → level-1 residual chain → Lorentzian argmin → SID digits 1..L → Stage-3 sequence. Behaviour off (alpha = 0, w = 0) feeds the raw item point into the same curved chain; geometry off (kappa → 0) keeps the same twins but replaces the consensus and every assignment with Euclidean ones. Both switches change the SID assignment itself, not an accessory loss.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If behaviourally interchangeable items should share the level-1 token, then smoothing the quantiser input along successor-profile edges will (a) raise the share of successor-linked pairs that share a level-1 code, (b) raise the issue-#126 Q_H recomputed on the new SIDs, and (c) push the single frozen Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. ideas.hyperbolic_location: In Stage-2 quantisation and at the encoder→quantiser interface: the lift, the behaviour consensus point, the codebook parameterisation, the assignment cost and the residual chain are all on the hyperboloid; the decoder maps back with log_0.

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. The elimination of A/D converters and implementation of block-coding directly over analog blocks of pixels in such sensors can be attractive both in terms of area savings and power consumption. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation.
